audio.author: Garuda1982, field recording with a Zoom H2n (Freesound 420387, CC0)
audio.performers: A bullroarer: a slat of wood on a cord, swung overhead. The oldest known ones are Magdalenian, carved from bone and reindeer antler; one from La Roche de Birol at Lalinde, in the Dordogne like Lascaux, is about 15,000 years old. This is a modern one, recorded outdoors.
audio.notes: Bullroarers (rhombes) are among the few Palaeolithic instruments that survive: decorated bone and antler slats pierced at one end, from Magdalenian sites including La Roche de Birol (Lalinde, Dordogne, c. 15,000 BP, Musée d'Archéologie nationale) and Abri de Laugerie-Basse; replicas sound exactly like wooden ones, since the sound is made by the slat spinning in the air. No free recording of a replica exists (Commons has none; the Marsoulas conch recording in Fritz et al. 2021, Science Advances, is CC BY-NC). This 26.8 s CC0 field recording of a modern bullroarer by Garuda1982 on Freesound, played in a loop at the Megaloceros of Lascaux, the first Magdalenian work on the lane.
